title: The New Year swim
summary: Every first of January, a group of neighbours jumps into the cold sea, and this year Iván decides to join them.
paragraphs: Every year on the first of January, at twelve o'clock exactly, a group of people from Iván's town runs into the sea. It doesn't matter if it's windy, cloudy or raining. The water is usually about fourteen degrees, which is not freezing, but it feels like it when you have just left a warm bed after a New Year's party. Iván had watched them from the beach for years, wearing a coat and holding a hot coffee, and he had always thought they were a little crazy.

This year, he made a {{resolution}}: to try something that frightened him. His neighbour Charo, who was sixty-eight and had done the New Year swim for twenty years, offered to help him prepare. "Don't just jump in on the day," she said. "Your body needs to get used to it." From the beginning of December, they went to the beach twice a week. On the first day, Iván only put his feet in. A week later, he went in up to his knees. By Christmas, he could stay in the water for two minutes.

Charo explained why she did it. After her husband died, she had felt tired and sad for a long time. A friend took her to the beach one cold morning and told her to get into the water. "It was terrible," she said, "for about ten seconds. Then I felt more awake than I had for months." Scientists, she told him, think that cold water can improve mood and help people sleep, though they are still studying exactly why. "But I don't need a scientist," she said, laughing. "I just need my towel and a good {{breakfast}} afterwards."

On the first of January, there were about two hundred people on the beach, many of them in {{fancy dress}}. There was a man dressed as a penguin, a family in matching red hats and a group of firefighters. At twelve o'clock, someone blew a {{whistle}}, and everybody ran screaming into the waves. The cold hit Iván like a wall. For a second he couldn't breathe. Then, just as Charo had promised, the {{shock}} went away, and he started laughing.

He was only in the water for three minutes. Afterwards, wrapped in a towel and drinking hot chocolate, he felt better than he had in years. Now Iván and Charo swim every Sunday, all year round. He has kept his resolution, and he has a new one: next year, he's going to wear a costume.

resolution.meaning: a promise to yourself to do or stop doing something, often at New Year

breakfast.meaning: the first meal of the day

fancy dress.meaning: special clothes that make you look like someone or something else

whistle.meaning: a small object that makes a high sound when you blow it

shock.meaning: a sudden strong feeling caused by something unexpected

questions.question: What did Iván think of the swimmers before?
options: That they were a little crazy
questions.explanation: He had always thought they were a little crazy.

questions.question: How did Charo help Iván prepare?
options: She gave him a special wetsuit.
They went to the beach twice a week so his body could get used to the cold.
She told him to drink hot coffee.
She took him to a doctor.
questions.explanation: From December they went twice a week, a little further into the water each time.

questions.question: Why did Charo start swimming in cold water?
options: A friend took her after a sad time, and it made her feel more awake.
She wanted to win a competition.
questions.explanation: After her husband died, a friend took her to the beach, and she felt more awake than in months.

questions.question: What is Iván's new resolution?
options: To wear a costume next year
To teach other people to swim
questions.explanation: Next year he's going to wear a costume.
